sector_model: Industrials, defense and nuclear electronics and engineered products (large mid): value on earnings and FCF, backlog and orders, pension and acquisition goodwill; not a bank or insurer model.
thesis: Curtiss-Wright (NYSE: CW). Q3 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-11-05) read in part (statements, backlog, debt, cash flow, MD&A orders and segments). Q3 sales 952.6M vs 869.2M (+9.6%); 9M 2,790.3M vs 2,551.4M (+9.4%); Q3 operating income 187.9M (19.7%, +60bp); 9M operating margin 18.9% (+120bp); 9M diluted EPS 11.31 vs 9.19. Backlog about 4.6B at 2026-09-30, about 90% to be recognized within 36 months; 9M new orders +379M with increases across all segments. TTM (FY25 + 9M26 - 9M25, USD): revenue 3,737.3M, net income 555.2M, OCF 708.7M, capex 118.9M, FCF 589.7M (excludes 25.5M capex grant proceeds in 9M26), SBC 29.0M. Close 456.53 (2026-11-18) x 36,272,260 shares (10-Q cover 2026-10-31) = 16.56B market cap = 29.8x TTM NI, FCF yield 3.6% (3.4% after SBC). Debt 957.1M (notes, 200M current) vs cash 281.1M, net debt about 676M, EV about 17.2B; 1B revolver to 2031. Buybacks 381.7M in 9M26 (2.3% of market cap) cut weighted diluted shares 2.1% y/y (36.99M vs 37.79M). The price implies sustained high single digit growth and margin expansion in defense and naval nuclear work; the filing shows orders and margins moving that way, so quality is evident but the valuation offers no visible discount; not shown to be mispriced.
counterthesis: 29.8x TTM earnings and a 3.6% FCF yield leave little room if naval or defense budgets slip or if margin expansion stalls. Naval and Power (44% of 9M sales) depends on U.S. Navy programs; customer concentration was not extracted. Working capital absorbed cash (receivables 1,049M vs 932M, inventories 716M vs 615M at year end). Goodwill 1,686M and intangibles 486M together equal 85% of equity (2,560M after 385M of buybacks). Pension prepaid asset 353M. Stock near highs (455 to 457) so any miss is punished.
invalidation: Invalidated if new orders turn negative, backlog shrinks, operating margin falls back below 17%, FCF stays near 3% yield while growth slows below mid single digits, or buybacks are funded by rising debt.
